decisions.rationale: Charizard leads to Mega Evolve immediately, setting permanent Drought sun to power Fire Blast and enable free Solar Beam. Weavile follows with Focus Sash for guaranteed priority Ice Shard revenge kills. Excadrill and Toxapex form the back core—Excadrill's Mold Breaker handles Steelix/Levitate targets, while Toxapex provides Regenerator defense and spreads Toxic Spikes/Haze to punish switches and stop setup.
decisions.notebook: Opponent likely runs Mega Gengar Shadow Tag trap + Grimmsnarl Prankster screens. Our answer: immediate Mega Charizard Y sun offense. Weavile Focus Sash priority revenge. Excadrill Mold Breaker irreplaceable coverage (Earthquake OHKOs Bastiodon 4x, hits through Levitate). Toxapex defensive anchor walls physical attackers. Rotom-Wash pivots via Volt Switch, threatens Slowbro/Empoleon. Venusaur is endgame cleaner—Chlorophyll under Drought + Growth SpA makes Leaf Storm an OHKO on Empoleon and heavy damage to all. Save Rotom-Wash and Venusaur for mid/late game when sun is established and hazards are up.

decisions.rationale: Lead Slowbro (Fire resist 0.5x, Psychic 2x on Venusaur/Toxapex) + Grimmsnarl (Prankster Fake Out +3 flinches Weavile Ice Shard +1, sets screens). Gengar has no Protect and is OHKO'd by Weavile Knock Off (Dark 2x, 96-137%), so bench it to trap Charizard later with Thunderbolt. Arcanine back for Intimidate and Wild Charge/Flare Blitz. Box Empoleon/Lucario.

reflections.summary: Lost because Toxapex was the sole defensive anchor and fell to a critical Wild Charge from Arcanine on turn 8. The team preview over-committed to sun offense (Mega Charizard-Y + Weavile) without adequate defensive redundancy or a Steel- or Water-type answer to Arcanine's physical assault. Weavile and Charizard were picked off early, Excadrill died to Flare Blitz after hitting Arcanine, and Slowbro contributed little beyond repeated Psychics into Protect. Baneful Bunker PP eventually ran too low to sustain.
reflections.adjustment: Swap Slowbro (or Grimmsnarl) for Empoleon in the team four. Empoleon's Steel typing resists Flare Blitz, neutralizes Arcanine's STAB combination, and Flash Cannon/Ice Beam threaten both Arcanine and Grimmsnarl. This gives the team a second reliable defensive pivot that doesn't rely solely on Toxapex stalling.
reflections.notebook: Opponent runs Reflect support via Grimmsnarl (LightClay, Prankster). Arcanine: Flare Blitz/Wild Charge/ExtremeSpeed/Protect, Intimidate, Shuca Berry — physically aggressive pivot. Slowbro: Regenerator Calm Mind with Psychic/Scald/SlackOff/Protect; Sitrus Berry burned. Gengar: Timid NastyPlot set (Thunderbolt/ShadowBall/DazzlingGleam) with Mega Gengar available. Empoleon (Leftovers, Torrent) and Lucario (ExpertBelt, InnerFocus) remain unpunished bench options; Empoleon's Steel typing is the key adjustment for game 2 to handle Arcanine and add defensive depth.

reflections.summary: Won via early momentum: Grimmsnarl Fake Out flinched Weavile, Play Rough KO; Gengar Thunderbolt revenge killed Mega Charizard Y after Solar Beam charge; Arcanine Flare Blitz KO'd Excadrill; Slowbro/Arcanine broke Toxapex. Four brought (Gengar/Slowbro/Arcanine/Grimmsnarl) suited opponent's sun/ground core; Gengarite holder not evolved as Gengar fainted early to Mold Breaker EQ, which was acceptable.
reflections.adjustment: Avoid contact moves into Toxapex while Baneful Bunker active (Arcanine poisoned T7); use Slowbro non-contact Psychic until Bunker cooldown then Wild Charge. Next game anticipate Rotom-Wash Trick disabling items.
